questions.prompt: Which measure describes the delay before data starts arriving, rather than how much data the link can carry?
questions.explanation: Latency is the delay before anything arrives; bandwidth is link capacity and throughput is what you actually achieved.

questions.prompt: Two laptops connected by a single cable already form a network.
questions.explanation: A network is just nodes connected by links that can exchange data, so two nodes and one link qualify.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.
pairs: The maximum capacity of a link
A device with an address that can send or receive data
questions.explanation: Bandwidth is the size of the pipe, latency is the delay, throughput is the real rate you got, and a node is any addressable device on the network.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in the order they happen as a browser's HTTP request is encapsulated for sending.
items: The Application layer builds the HTTP request
The Transport layer adds a TCP header (a segment)
The Internet layer adds an IP header (a packet)
The Link layer adds an Ethernet header and trailer (a frame)
questions.explanation: Each layer wraps what the layer above handed it, so headers are added from Transport down to Link, with the Link header outermost.

questions.prompt: Which of these are costs or properties of packet switching?
choices: Packets can arrive out of order
A dedicated path is reserved before any data is sent
Reserved capacity sits idle when nobody is talking
answers: Packets can arrive out of order
questions.explanation: Independent packets can take different routes, arrive out of order, and each carries its own header. Reserving a path and idle reserved capacity describe circuit switching.

questions.prompt: How many layers does the TCP/IP model have?
questions.explanation: TCP/IP uses four layers: Link, Internet, Transport, and Application.

questions.prompt: How many usable host addresses are in a /26 IPv4 subnet?
questions.explanation: A /26 leaves 32 - 26 = 6 host bits, so 2^6 - 2 = 62 usable hosts after removing the network and broadcast addresses.

questions.prompt: A packet's destination MAC address stays the same for its whole trip across the internet.
questions.explanation: MAC addresses only matter for one hop at a time; each hop rewrites the Link-layer addresses while the IP addresses stay the same.

questions.prompt: How many bits long is an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits, versus 32 bits for IPv4, which is what fixes address exhaustion.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the IP header field that a router decrements at each hop to stop packets from looping forever?
questions.explanation: TTL (time to live) is reduced at every router, and the packet is discarded when it reaches zero.

questions.prompt: Match each network component to its job.
pairs: Rewrites private addresses to a public address
questions.explanation: Switches work inside a network, routers connect networks, NAT translates private to public addresses, and DNS resolves names.

questions.prompt: How does a NAT router keep track of which private device a reply belongs to when many share one public IP?
choices: It keeps a translation table that also tracks port numbers
It gives each device a different public IP
It broadcasts the reply to every device
It uses the devices' MAC addresses on the internet
questions.answer: It keeps a translation table that also tracks port numbers
questions.explanation: NAT records each outgoing connection (address and port) in an internal table and uses it to send the response back to the right device.

questions.prompt: Put the TCP three-way handshake in order.
questions.explanation: The client opens with SYN, the server answers with SYN-ACK, and the client confirms with ACK.

questions.prompt: What is the highest valid port number? (Ports are 16-bit numbers.)
questions.explanation: A 16-bit number ranges from 0 to 2^16 - 1, which is 65,535.

questions.prompt: UDP sends data without first establishing a connection.
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless: no handshake, no delivery guarantee, which makes it fast.

questions.prompt: Match each HTTP status code to its meaning.
questions.explanation: 2xx means success, 3xx redirects, 4xx client errors, and 5xx server errors.

questions.prompt: Explain how HTTPS protects a request from someone sniffing traffic on the network, compared with plain HTTP.
rubric: Says HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS
Says a sniffer sees only unreadable ciphertext, not the content
Mentions the TLS handshake sets up the keys or authenticates the server
questions.model: HTTPS is HTTP sent inside a TLS connection. After the TLS handshake the two sides share keys and all traffic is encrypted, so someone sniffing sees only unreadable ciphertext instead of the request contents that plain HTTP would expose.
questions.explanation: TLS adds encryption (and server authentication) under HTTP, so captured packets no longer reveal the content.

questions.prompt: HTTP is stateless, meaning the server treats each request independently without remembering earlier ones by default.
questions.explanation: Statelessness is why cookies and similar mechanisms are needed to carry state between requests.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of a minimal TCP server in order.
items: Bind it to a local port
questions.explanation: A server creates, binds, listens, accepts, exchanges data, then closes.

questions.prompt: In the traced client-server exchange, what call in the client's code triggers the TCP three-way handshake?
questions.explanation: connect() starts the SYN / SYN-ACK / ACK exchange before any message data is sent.

questions.prompt: Match each socket operation to what it does.
pairs: Associates the socket with a local port
Waits for incoming connection attempts (server only)
Blocks until a client connects, then returns a connection
Client initiates a connection to an address and port
questions.explanation: Servers bind, listen, and accept; clients call connect.

questions.prompt: Which protocol does `ping` use to test whether a destination is reachable?
questions.explanation: ping sends ICMP echo messages, a lightweight Internet-layer protocol for diagnostics.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its description.
pairs: Forging the source address of traffic
Capturing traffic passing by on a network
Secretly relaying or altering traffic between two parties
Allows or blocks traffic based on rules
questions.explanation: The first three are attacks defenders must understand; a firewall is the rule-based filter that helps defend against them.

questions.prompt: traceroute finds each router hop by sending packets with increasing TTL values.
questions.explanation: Each router that discards an expired packet reveals itself, so TTL 1, 2, 3... maps the path hop by hop.
